flashcards.q: Three properties of a usable North Star metric?
flashcards.a: (1) Measures customer value received, not activity performed; (2) a sum, not a ratio (ratios hide absolute decline); (3) predicts revenue with a nameable lag validated on historical cohorts. Example: weekly active learners completing an assessed activity.

flashcards.q: What does AARRR stand for and in what order should you DIAGNOSE?
flashcards.a: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue (McClure's pirate metrics). Diagnose retention first (consumer W4 <~5-10% means leaking bucket), then activation (funnels commonly lose 60-80% of signups pre-first-action), then acquisition efficiency.

flashcards.q: When does a leading indicator legitimately earn the title?
flashcards.a: Only after cohort validation: 8+ historical periods showing candidate movement followed by outcome movement, stable across segments. NPS famously fails as a revenue predictor at segment level despite popularity - useful signal, mislabeled forecaster.

flashcards.q: State Goodhart's Law and give the canonical support-ticket failure.
flashcards.a: When a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure. Mechanism: optimization pressure concentrates on the proxy; the proxy-goal gap becomes waste. Support teams close tickets unread to hit resolution-time SLAs because closure is measured and comprehension isn't.

flashcards.q: Name three Goodhart defenses and one cost each.
flashcards.a: Paired counter-metrics (cost: complexity, contradictory signals); human quality sampling of ~5% random slices (cost: reviewer time/bias); composite indices like LinkedIn's OTE (cost: weights become political). Also rotating targets/holdouts. Gaming strategies evolve, so revisit defenses annually.

flashcards.q: How many guardrails per experiment and what happens if you over-guardrail?
flashcards.a: 2-4 numeric thresholds agreed BEFORE launch (e.g., p95 latency <= +10%, complaint rate <0.5%, relevance >= -1%). Over-guardrailing freezes motion: ten hard gates mean most experiments ship nothing and teams stop trying. Park secondaries in monitoring, not launch gates.

flashcards.q: Activation 28%, W4 19%: where does engineering effort go and why?
flashcards.a: Usually activation: +6pts on 28% is ~21% relative lift multiplying EVERY downstream stage, while W4 moves affect only retained cohorts. Precondition: retention curve flattens (smile). If it never flattens, fixing activation multiplies leak - fix PMF signals first.

flashcards.q: Why is DAU/MAU dangerous as a North Star?
flashcards.a: Ratios mask absolute decline (both terms can shrink while ratio rises), conflate frequency with value across product categories, and game via hollow notification opens. Use sum-form NS for value delivered; keep stickiness ratios as diagnostics only.

flashcards.q: Sean Ellis test: question, threshold, meaning.
flashcards.a: Ask active users 'How would you feel if you could no longer use this product?' ~40% answering 'very disappointed' historically separated scaling from struggling startups in Ellis's cross-startup dataset. Calibrate your own threshold against your own history.

flashcards.q: Your recsys shows +25% engagement but relevance -12% and next-day return -9%. Ship?
flashcards.a: Net ~+4pts is noise-level once guardrail losses are netted: BLOCK/iterate. The engagement gain likely reflects clickbait drift exploiting impulse rather than long-run value - that's why delayed outcomes (next-day/week return) outrank same-session clicks in decision weight.

flashcards.q: What enters an AI feature's metric tree that classic trees lacked?
flashcards.a: Cost-per-outcome as a first-class input (token COGS makes engagement-without-economics fatal) plus over-reliance/correction-rate guardrails (e.g., % learners requesting hints on >70% of attempts). Engagement alone stopped being obviously good.

flashcards.q: When do you retire a metric?
flashcards.a: When its causal link to the North Star broke (verify annually via cohort regression), it's been gamed past informativeness, two owners report irreconcilable definitions, or it hasn't informed a real decision in two quarters. Archive raw events, delete the KPI - attention surface is the scarce resource.
